A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CosPress and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Content can be matched reliably across the shortened title, reformatting, and relocations.

before.justification: V2 reports original distillation, classification, segmentation, robustness, OOD detection, and ablation results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds alternative-teacher results and four-seed summaries for selected ImageNet comparisons.

M1.justification: The teacher compression head, dimensionality-reduction objective, cosine student loss, and gradient-freezing procedure are retained. V3's Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Reported dataset and task coverage remains unchanged, including ImageNet, fine-grained classification, Pascal VOC, and the robustness and OOD suites. New Table 8 varies teacher configurations on ImageNet. The specialist generalisation and OOD evaluations already appeared in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: Proteus, Proteus-VkD, the Proteus patch-loss variant, DINOv2, DeiT, NAT, and CeiT retain their corresponding comparisons. New Table 8 uses the existing Proteus comparator with additional teacher configurations.

E3.justification: New Table 8 evaluates DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with registers and CLIP ViT-B/16 teachers, using ViT-T/14 and ViT-T/16 students respectively. These experiments use the existing ImageNet hyperparameters. Additional details about retained experiments are disclosures, without an established revision to their settings.

E4.justification: Table 8 adds a check of whether CosPress's advantage persists across different teacher architectures and pretraining approaches. Existing component, orthogonality, larger-teacher, loss-weighting, loss-metric, and temperature analyses remain. Moving specialist robustness analyses into Section 5 adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports means and standard deviations across four random seeds for Proteus and CosPress ViT-Ti/14. V2 provides point estimates without a run count, so an increase in runs cannot be established. V3 claims statistical significance without specifying a significance test.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces earlier point estimates with four-seed summaries: Proteus tiny-model kNN changes from 73.1 to 73.0, and CosPress linear accuracy from 76.8 to 76.6. New Table 8 reports CosPress versus Proteus linear accuracies of 76.4 versus 75.1 with the register teacher and 72.0 versus 71.4 with CLIP. Other matched numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 adds Definition 1 for approximate orthogonality. Its accompanying reasoning incorrectly reverses v2's stated implication, claiming approximate right-orthogonality suffices for left-orthogonality. Lemma 1 and its appendix proof retain the original direction; the remaining mathematical development is substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: cosine-preserving teacher compression, more faithful transfer of foundation-model properties, and effective specialist-model training. Additional teacher experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New Section 6 connects angular preservation to superposition and explicitly questions whether the remaining generalisation gap arises from training data or methodology. Section 3 adds a batch-size scaling qualification. V3 also softens the interpretation of Proteus-VkD's performance and removes v2's mixup/cutmix explanations for specialist generalisation and OOD improvements.

D1.justification: V3 discloses AdamW, cosine decay, five warmup epochs, three augmentation views, and RandAugment for distillation. It adds specialist training/warmup budgets, including 3000/100 epochs for Oxford Pets, and Algorithm 1. These improve documentation of retained procedures; the code-access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds dimensionality-reduction positioning and citations connecting angular representations to superposition, alongside references supporting the added implementation details and register teacher. It removes the statement that Proteus is the only known approach distilling foundation models from scratch. The principal comparison with Proteus remains.

P1.justification: V3 shortens the title, repairs grammatical problems, expands selected explanations, adds a Discussion section, and integrates two existing specialist analyses into Section 5. Most prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. V2's radar Figure 1 is removed; the other three figures are retained and renumbered. V3 adds Table 8 and Algorithm 1 and moves Tables S11–S12 into the main text as Tables 12–13.

improvement.justification: Four-seed reporting and alternative-teacher comparisons modestly strengthen empirical support, while explicit training settings and pseudocode improve reproducibility. Most evidence remains unchanged. These gains are partly offset by the new contradictory explanation of Lemma 1, yielding a limited overall improvement.
